description:
Attach a file you made in Odie's workspace (with the shell or a skill). A picture (png, jpg, webp, gif, svg)
is shown under your reply, a video (mp4, webm, mov) or a sound (mp3, m4a, wav) plays there, anything else is
a download card. `path` is inside the workspace: relative to it, or absolute.
name: attach_file

description:
Check quarterly results you read from a web page (any company outside the US) and get a ready-made
```odie-blocks board to paste unchanged. Numbers exactly as the page shows them, in its unit.
quarters: 5 labels oldest first, like "Jun 2025" (the latest 4 plus the one a year before the latest).
currency: a symbol, e.g. ₹ or €. scale: the page's unit, "Cr", "M" or "B". Every list has one value per quarter.
expenses/interest/operating_profit: as the table names them (a bank's Financing Profit is operating_profit).
source_url: the page you read. filings_url: the exchange filings page if the page links one.
If a check fails it says which; re-read the table and call again.
name: build_report

description:
Write a skill into staging and check it (its code is read, never run). name: lowercase-with-hyphens.
description: one line, what it does and when to use it. instructions: the SKILL.md body in Markdown.
tools_code: the whole tools.py, or "" for an instructions-only skill. blocks: the block kinds it draws.
Returns "Ready to install" or the problems to fix; call again with fixes until it's ready.
name: draft_skill

description: Read one remembered entry by its title (as listed in 'What you remember'). Partial titles work when unique.
name: fetch_memory

description:
Remove one remembered entry by its title, when the user says it's wrong or no longer wanted ("stop watching
for the passport email", "forget that"). Its text is kept in the memory's history.
name: forget_memory

description:
Install a drafted skill that draft_skill said is ready, with the version it gave. The user sees an approval card
with the skill's text and code; it installs (and its code is allowed) only when the user taps Approve.
name: install_skill

description: The user's trackers: what each checks, how often, its status and the latest result.
name: list_trackers

description:
Adds an event to the Mac's calendar (the first writable one, or `calendar_name`). Local times. Returns the
event's id and the calendar it went into.
name: mac_calendar_add

description:
Events in every calendar on this Mac between two local times ("2026-10-21T00:00", "2026-10-28T00:00"):
id, title, start, end, where, attendees, calendar, all_day.
name: mac_calendar_events

description:
New mail in the Mac's Mail app since a local time ("2026-10-21T09:00"), newest first, at most `limit`:
id, from, subject, at, snippet, attachments. Read one in full with mac_mail_read. This is Apple Mail only: a mail
that isn't here may be in another connected mail app, so load its skill and look there before saying it isn't
found. Never search the disk for mail.
name: mac_mail_new

description:
One message from the Mac's Mail app in full, by the id mac_mail_new gave ("mac:123"). An id without "mac:"
belongs to another mail app: read it with that app's tools.
name: mac_mail_read

description:
Saves one attachment of a Mail message (by the message's id and the attachment's name) into Odie's workspace;
returns its path.
name: mac_mail_save_attachment

description: Adds a reminder to the Reminders app, due at a local time, in the default list or `list_name`.
name: mac_reminder_add

description: Open reminders in the Reminders app due before a local time: id, title, due, list.
name: mac_reminders

description:
Make the audio story the user chose in the guided start: a narrator, character voices, ambience, effects and
music, posted to this chat as one file. Call it once, after the cast form. A separate writer writes the script and
chooses the sound in the background; it sees only what you pass here.
title: the story's title (short). genre: as the user chose it ("horror"). premise: the pitch or idea they chose,
a sentence or two.
cast: [{id, name, voice, about}] for the narrator and each character: id a short plain word ("keeper"), name as
the listener knows them ("The keeper"), voice a value from story_voices, about one line on who they are.
narrator: the id of who tells it: "narrator" for an outside storyteller (then in the cast as id "narrator"), or a
character's id to tell it in the first person.
accent: as chosen ("British"). minutes: 2 to 15 (the user's length, else 5). sound_level: 10 to 40, how loud the
ambience is when no one speaks; it drops lower under the voices (the slider's value, else 25). brief: anything else the user asked for (tone, an
ending, who it's for).
It returns at once. {"error": …}: fix exactly that and call again. {"result": …}: reply in one or two lines as it
says.
name: make_audio_story

description:
Make a designed deck: a PDF and an editable PowerPoint with slide previews, posted to this chat. A separate
writer writes the slides from your brief, in the background; it can't see this chat, the user's notes, memory or
the web, and can't search for photos.
topic: what it's about, short ("A weekend in Coorg", "Nvidia's Q2").
brief: the angle, the slides' points in order, the facts it must use, and the photo addresses with their credits
that find_images or the browser gave you (only those can go on the slides). Up to 6,000 characters.
theme: editorial (dark, great with photos), minimal (clean white: research, business), warm (cream), bold (strong
colour: pitches).
revise: to change a deck made earlier, its name ("Meghalaya Trip Guide"); the brief then says what to change.
sources: what the user gave, passed to the writer word for word (never retype it): "my message" (the user's
latest message), a note's name or path in their vault, or a text file's path in Odie's workspace. Up to 5.
It returns at once. {"error": …}: fix exactly that and call again. {"result": …}: the deck is being made; reply in
one or two lines as the result says, and don't repeat the brief.
name: make_deck

description:
Make a Word document from Markdown and attach it to the chat: "#" and "##" headings, paragraphs with **bold**
and *italic*, "- " and "1. " lists, "| a | b |" tables, "---" for a page break. `title` names the file (else the
first heading).
name: make_document

description:
Make a file for the user from the chat: a spreadsheet (.csv), notes (.md or .txt), a web page (.html), data
(.json), a calendar event (.ics) or a drawing (.svg, shown right under your reply; for a drawing in the reply
itself an ```odie-svg block needs no file). `name` is the file name with its extension ("Goa packing list.csv");
`content` is the whole file. The card appears under your reply. For slides (PowerPoint) or a Word document,
load the documents skill instead.
name: make_file

description:
Make a podcast the user can play in this chat: two hosts (a woman, then a man) talking a topic through,
NotebookLM style. A separate writer writes the script from your brief, in the background; it can't see this chat,
the user's notes, memory or the web.
topic: what it's about, short ("How vaccines train the immune system", "Our session on the move to Pune").
minutes: its length, from 1 to 10: the user's length, else 4.
brief: the angle, the key points in order, and the facts from this chat or the notes it must use (for a podcast
of this conversation: its decisions, questions and surprises). Up to 6,000 characters.
sources: what the user gave, passed to the writer word for word (never retype it): "my message" (the user's
latest message), a note's name or path in their vault, or a text file's path in Odie's workspace. Up to 5.
It returns at once. {"error": …}: fix exactly that and call again. {"result": …}: the podcast is being made; reply
in one or two lines as the result says, and don't repeat the brief.
name: make_podcast

description:
Research a question in the background and post a report (a Markdown file) to this chat: a separate writer
searches the web and the user's notes, reads what matters and writes the answer with its sources. Use it for
anything time-consuming that is mostly reading: research, look into, compare, find out, a report on. The writer
can't see this chat or the user's memory.
topic: what to find out, short ("Which kettle to buy for a family of four").
brief: the question as the user means it, what matters to them, what is known already (facts from this chat),
what to skip, and where to look (their notes, sites they trust). Up to 6,000 characters.
sources: what the user gave, passed to the writer word for word (never retype it): "my message" (the user's
latest message), a note's name or path in their vault, or a text file's path in Odie's workspace. Up to 5.
It returns at once. {"error": …}: fix exactly that and call again (in a private chat, tell the user what it says).
{"result": …}: the research is being made; reply in one or two lines as the result says, and don't repeat the
brief.
name: make_research

description:
Make a narrated, animated explainer video that plays in this chat. A separate writer makes the narration and
the animation from your brief, in the background; it can't see this chat, the user's notes, memory or the web.
topic: what the video is about, short ("How attention works").
minutes: its length, from 1 to 6: the user's length, else 2.
brief: the plan: who it's for and their level, the key points in order, the look, examples, numbers or formulas
that must appear, and any facts you found. Up to 20,000 characters.
sources: what the user gave, passed to the writer word for word (never retype it): "my message" (the user's
latest message), a note's name or path in their vault, or a text file's path in Odie's workspace. Up to 5.
images: pictures for the film, at most 20, each one line "address — what it shows": the address a tool gave
(https://… from find_images, photo:<id>, upload:<id>, screenshot:<id>), then what the picture shows, its mood, its
orientation if unusual, and a web picture's credit in brackets at the end. The writer sees only these words.
For a reel, find web pictures and clips only when the topic needs a real one (a place, a person, a real thing);
the writer draws the rest.
clips: short stock clips, at most 6, the same way, with the https:// address find_clips gave.
sounds: leave true; false only when the user asks for no sound effects.
voice_name: leave empty; only when the user asks for a voice, one of the Settings engine's voices.
style: leave empty; only when the user says how the narrator should sound, one line up to 300 characters, like
"Curious science narrator. Calm, but lift slightly at the payoff. Slow down on numbers." Only OpenAI's voices
follow it.
aspect: leave empty (a wide video); "vertical" when the user says insta, reel, shorts, vertical or mobile (a
1080 x 1920 reel; only the frame changes, its length is still `minutes`). Never put the aspect in the brief.
timed_segment_seconds: leave empty; only when the brief says a segment must last exactly N seconds (a countdown
character's 60 seconds inside a longer video): N. The writer marks that segment, and Odie fits its voice to exactly
N seconds, first word to last; the rest of the video keeps its natural length.
brand_kit: leave empty; only when a skill says to use its brand kit: that skill's name. The kit's fixed look,
sounds and opening and closing scenes go in as they are, and the writer draws around them.
script: leave empty; only for a dialogue video the user wrote: "my message" when they pasted it, else their
script's note name or path, or a workspace file ("## Scene: …" headings, "SPEAKER: line" lines). The writer
stages it word for word; never retype it, and the brief then says only the look and the cast's appearance.
voices: with a script only, a voice for every speaker but the narrator: [{"id": "anna", "name": <a voice of the
Settings engine>}]; with a cast, only to change a sheet's voice for this video.
cast: with a script, the folder of the work's character sheets when the user has one (a path in their vault,
"Stories/The lighthouse/cast", or a full path): each character's look, voice and ages come from it.
look: with a script, the work's style file when the user has one (a note or file: palette, lens, grain, period).
It returns at once. {"error": …}: fix exactly that and call again. {"result": …}: the video is being made; reply
in one or two lines as the result says, and don't repeat the brief.
name: make_video

description:
Price history for a stock, index, currency or commodity, with a chart. symbol: a name or ticker, e.g. NIFTY,
SENSEX, BANK NIFTY, RELIANCE, TCS.NS, AAPL, gold, USDINR. period: 1d, 5d, 1mo, 3mo, 6mo, 1y, 2y, 5y or 10y
("last week" = 5d; any other, like 3y, gets the next longer one).
Returns a summary and a ```odie-blocks block to paste into the reply unchanged so the app draws the chart.
name: market_history

description: Current date and time in the user's timezone.
name: now

description:
Everything Odie can do right now, read live: built-in abilities, skills, connected apps, models and providers,
voice, active trackers, what runs on its own, visual blocks, and how to add more.
name: odie_features

description:
A US-listed company's last 4 quarters from SEC filings: revenue, margins, profit, cash, with a ready-made
```odie-blocks board to paste unchanged. company: a name or ticker, e.g. Qualys, QLYS, Tenable, Apple.
name: quarterly_financials

description:
The SKILL.md and tools.py of an existing skill: one of the user's (to change it) or a built-in one such as
stocks (as a worked example).
name: read_skill

description: Run a shell command on this computer (zsh). The user sees the exact command and directory and approves it first. Use for files, git, scripts, system questions. cwd defaults to their home and must stay under it. Output is capped at 8 KB and 60 seconds.
name: run_shell

description: Keyword search across everything remembered about the user. Use when the index has no obvious title.
name: search_memories

description:
How to write a Odie skill: the SKILL.md and tools.py rules, the visual blocks and icons the app can draw,
and the tool names already taken. Call this first when building or changing a skill.
name: skill_guide

description:
Read text aloud as one short voice memo the user can play right in the chat: the player appears under your
reply. Use it when the user asks for a voice memo, a voice note, or to hear something. `script` is what to
say, as plain speech, at most about 4,000 characters (some 4 minutes); it's read in the voice chosen in
Settings. `voice_name` (optional) is another voice for this one memo, only when the user asks for one ("a
man's voice"): a voice of the same engine as the Settings voice, by name ("Michael"); another engine's voice
is refused with the list to pick from. `title` is short (optional). The result's `path` is the saved WAV file
(kept), for a skill's own narration, e.g. with ffmpeg. When it works, reply in one short line; don't repeat
the script. Not for a story, a radio play or anything with several voices, sound or music: that is
make_audio_story (the audio-story skill), never several speak calls stitched together. A podcast with two
hosts is make_podcast (the podcast skill).
name: speak

description: Stop a tracker for good (the user can also pause or stop it on Today).
name: stop_tracker

description:
The voices for an audio story's cast form, for the voice engine chosen in Settings.
accent: "American", "British" or "Indian", as the user chose it with the story. Without one, it returns the
accents this engine offers, for that question.
Returns {"engine", "accent", "options"}: options is the voices for that accent (and, on Phonon, its character
voices: a pirate captain, a witch, an old keeper), each {value, label, note, preview}. Paste options exactly as
given as the options of every voice select in the cast form, previews and all; use a `value` as the voice in
make_audio_story. {"error": …}: choose as it says.
name: story_voices

description: Add an open thread to the user's ledger. kind: todo, reminder, followup, waiting. due / next_check: ISO datetime like 2026-10-01T11:00 (today's date from the context; naive times are the user's timezone). A reminder fires in the chat at `due`. source_ref: a message, thread or event id if there is one.
name: task_add

description: List ledger tasks. status: open (default), waiting, done, dropped, all.
name: task_list

description: Update a thread. status: done (the user handled it: paid, replied, finished), dropped (not needed), open, waiting. snooze_until: ISO datetime to hide it and remind again then. next_check: ISO datetime for a follow-up.
name: task_update

description:
Start a background tracker: Odie checks `check` on a schedule and tells the user (push + a line in Chat) when it
matters. title: short, e.g. "Arsenal v Spurs". check: what to look up, in plain words, e.g. "Arsenal vs Spurs
live score and match status". every: "5m", "15m", "2h", "1d", or times like "09:00", "mon 09:00", "weekdays 7:30".
notify: "change" (default: when the result changes), "always", or "condition" with condition, e.g. "price below 3000".
until: last date (YYYY-MM-DD); default 14 days. A check can also end it (match over, order delivered).
page: when this chat read a page of the user's own account (their orders), the address of the one page to check;
the user then decides whether the tracker may check it signed in.
name: track

description: Save something worth keeping about the user, people, preferences, projects or decisions. Reuse an existing title to update it; topic groups it (Identity, People, Projects, Health, Finance, ...).
name: update_memory

description:
Takes a watch item off Today (the user handled it, or doesn't want it) and closes the watch's thread for it.
why: in the user's words ("not interested", "replied from my phone").
name: watch_close

description:
A watch card's item on Today by its ref ("mail:<id>"): what it is, its suggestion and escape, and its
drafted reply when it has one. Use it when the user taps a card or asks about a watch item. To send a draft,
show it, then use the mail app's draft and send tools: the user approves the send.
name: watch_item

description: Read one web page (article, docs, listing) as text. Use after web_search when the snippet is not enough.
name: web_fetch

description: Search the web for current information: news, prices, weather, facts you are unsure of, anything after your training data. Returns numbered results with URLs (cite them) and real image URLs you can show.
name: web_search
